title: Proper coefficient compositor pasting for a refinement
statement: For a flat morphism a:Λ→Λ′ of commutative condensed rings, a compactification refinement r:c→d, and a bounded constructible Λ_X-object K, the scalar image of the original refinement followed by the projection for c equals the proper scalar mate for d.g, followed by Rd.g_* over Λ′ of the three-map paste (scalar image of the original normalized lift; proper scalar mate for r.hom; Rr_* over Λ′ of the open scalar comparison for c.i), followed by the original target compositor transported along r.hom_g. The compositor is evaluated at jc,! over Λ′ of the scalar-extended K. No scalar-extended constructibility is required. All constructions are the original maps of [def-pur-condensed-compact-support-projection-core].

source.place: Agent-formulated constituent of the coefficient/refinement compatibility argument in def-pur-condensed-compact-support-projection, original Steps 15–16. Not claimed as a literal theorem of Bhatt–Scholze.

proof.text: the refinement component is the proper direct image of its normalized open lift, followed by the pushforward compositor transported along `r.hom_g`. The projection component is the proper scalar mate followed by the proper image of the open scalar comparison. Expand these two component formulas and apply functoriality of scalar extension. The proper scalar mate respects composition of direct images: on the restriction side, both underived pastes are the same section map, with the same coefficient action by coefficient naturality. Derive this identity using the canonical right-derived comparisons; exact coefficient restriction preserves K-injective complexes because its scalar-extension left adjoint is exact. Uniqueness identifies these comparisons with the right-adjoint mates of the pullback compositors, namely `fieldPushComp`. Taking scalar mates therefore gives the proper coefficient compositor square. Transport it along `r.hom_g` by equality induction. Substitute it into the expanded refinement component. Naturality of `condensedPushScalar a d.g` moves the scalar image of the normalized lift past that mate. Naturality of the target compositor in the open scalar comparison moves that comparison before the compositor. Finally combine the three maps inside the final proper direct image by functoriality. This gives exactly the displayed paste. No scalar-extended constructibility hypothesis or coefficient compatibility of the normalized lift is used here.

theorem condensedPushScalar_refinement_factorization {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y}
    {c d : Compactification f} (r : c.Refinement d)
    (K : BoundedConstructible (condensedRingObj Λ X)) :
    (condensedScalar a Y).map ((fieldRefinement Λ r).app K) ≫
        (condensedProjection a c).app K.obj =
      (condensedPushScalar a d.g).app
          ((CondensedRing.openImmersionLowerShriek Λ d.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj K.obj) ≫
        (CondensedRing.lowerStar Λ' d.g).rightDerivedFunctor.map
          ((condensedScalar a d.Z).map (fieldProperOpen Λ r K) ≫
            (condensedPushScalar a r.hom).app
              ((CondensedRing.openImmersionLowerShriek Λ c.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj K.obj) ≫
            (CondensedRing.lowerStar Λ' r.hom).rightDerivedFunctor.map
              ((condensedOpenScalar a c.i).hom.app K.obj)) ≫
        ((fieldPushComp Λ' r.hom d.g).hom ≫
          eqToHom (congrArg (fieldDerivedLowerStar Λ') r.hom_g)).app
            ((CondensedRing.openImmersionLowerShriek Λ' c.i).mapDerivedCategory.obj
              ((condensedScalar a X).obj K.obj))
